nominal_positions.interpretation: The nose itself is the feminine referent.
Plural agreement with hairs in the commentators’ question.
Neuter agreement with the cloth in the nominative citation. The written neuter also occurs as the name for the bend, recorded among the interfaces.

source_policy_decisions.decision: The 5.2.30 direction and the 5.2.31 conventional name require distinct histories. The compared sources disagree locally on one letter in 30. No extra suffix or reading is credited for it.

Distinguish name of a bending, body part, associated person, and explicit analogies for hair and cloth. The verse establishes ordinary firm-grip usage. It does not itself derive that usage from a nose.
Exclude cillaḥ as the output of cik plus ka. Retain it on the different klinna eye route, and preserve the possessive-a explanation in the Bhāṣya. Record the cause of the English discrepancy as Open.
The fist is both the entity undergoing change and the grammatical subject on Mallinātha’s reading. The king is its possessor. The poem supplies new role evidence and zero new finite words.
Two edition addresses attest the same descriptive compound. Its masculine case belongs to the person. The standalone nasal derivative and internal compound member keep separate ownership.
